Thanks again for the call today, James — good to meet you and Sara. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned on pricing inputs: 

- Summary from call: ACME is evaluating Redwood to power the new in-app assistant and downstream summarization pipelines. Primary goals: predictable unit economics, <=200ms p50 generation for short queries, and support for longer customer transcripts (occasional long-context calls).

What we need from you to finalize a pricing estimate:
- Typical monthly token volume (or ranges) by workload: in-product assistant vs batch summarization.
- Average prompt tokens and average completion tokens per call for each workload (example: 120 prompt / 450 completion).
- Percent of requests that need extended context (8k / 32k / 128k).
- Target budget range and any enterprise procurement constraints (PO timing, preferred billing cadence).

If you can reply with those numbers or attach a quick sample export, I’ll produce a per-1M token pricing estimate and a committed-capacity option (Dedicated) showing potential savings. I attached a 1-page pricing template for reference.

Proposed next step: follow-up 30-min call with Jordan (our SE) to go over sample traces and confirm perf targets. Are you available next week?

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

Hi Marissa — thanks for the clear recap. Below are the numbers from our instrumented logs (last 30 days) and internal estimate ranges. I attached a CSV export (anonymized).

High-level volumes (monthly):
- In-product assistant (real-time): ~1.2M calls / month (~1.8B tokens/month estimated)
- Batch summarization (nightly/weekly): ~200k jobs / month (~600M tokens/month estimated)
- Total: ~2.4B tokens/month (~2,400M)

Average profile (real-time assistant):
- Avg prompt tokens: 120
- Avg completion tokens: 450
- Avg tokens per call: 570

Average profile (batch summarization):
- Avg prompt tokens: 1,800 (long transcript prefix)
- Avg completion tokens: 1,200
- Avg tokens per job: 3,000

Context-length needs (estimated percentage of requests):
- 8k context sufficient: 70% of calls (most short assistant queries + smaller summaries)
- 32k context needed: 25% (longer transcripts, multi-turn history)
- 128k context needed: 5% (very long call transcripts / legal reviews)

Budget range: $6,000 - $10,000 / month (initial committed budget). For evaluation we are targetting an effective unit cost of about $10 - $15 per 1M tokens (but open to recommendations if committed capacity materially changes unit economics).

Attachment: acme_token_report.csv (stub)

Let me know if you want additional breakdown by endpoint or a sample of traces. We’re available Tues/Thurs next week for a SE sync.

—James
James Li
Product Lead, Conversational AI
Acme Corporation

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: James Li <james.li@acme.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Mar 2026 11:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: ACME pricing + context length profiling

James — this is great, thanks for the detail and the CSV. I pulled together a preliminary estimate and a few configuration notes for cost optimization. See the attached PDF estimate for two options: Hosted API (pay-as-you-go) and Dedicated (reserved capacity). Key highlights below.

Preliminary unit economics (illustrative):
- Baseline hosted (no commitment): $22 / 1M tokens (avg across token lengths)
- Committed / Dedicated (12mo): $12 / 1M tokens (base tier) with additional volume tiers that can get to ~$9 / 1M at high volumes
- Quantization / batching discount: we commonly see 10-25% effective token cost reduction depending on workload; with your mix I used a conservative 15% effective reduction

Using your 2.4B tokens/mo estimate (guesstimate across both workloads):
- Hosted: ~$52,800 / month
- Dedicated (12mo): ~$28,800 / month (after estimated optimization)

Context-length sizing notes (for pricing + infra):
- 70% under 8k: route to smaller model variants and standard batching — good latency; lowest cost
- 25% need 32k: plan for a 32k optimized model family (some increased cost per token due to inference overhead)
- 5% need 128k: we recommend isolating these as dedicated pipeline (batch/off-peak) or tailored Dedicated nodes to avoid p99 latency impact.

Next steps I propose:
1) SE deep-dive (Jordan) to review a small set of traces (you can mark redacted samples in the Drive link).
2) I’ll produce a formal TCO spreadsheet that shows per-1M pricing by context bin (8k, 32k, 128k) and the effect of 12/24-month commitments.
3) If the math looks good, we’ll schedule procurement + PO templates for Dedicated.

Suggested times: Tues 3/3 10:00-10:30 PT or Thurs 3/5 14:00-14:30 PT (Jordan is available both). Which works best?

Attachment: redwood_pricing_estimate.pdf (stub)

Thanks — will follow up with the formal spreadsheet once we confirm the SE slot.

Best,
Marissa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
